claims.text: The starting alloy is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a homogenized, polycrystalline, single-phase FCC state.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively high stacking-fault energy.
Relatively high stacking-fault energy suppresses deformation twinning in CoCrFeNiTi.
Suppression of deformation twinning limits the work-hardening capacity of CoCrFeNiTi.
Limited twinning and work hardening govern the alloy's combination of low hardness, low strength, and favorable ductility.
The proposed intervention replaces 10% of the Ti sublattice with Mn, denoted CoCrFeNiTi0.9Mn0.1.
Adding Mn lowers the stacking-fault energy of the modified alloy.
Lower stacking-fault energy reduces the critical stress for partial-dislocation emission.
Lower stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning.
The increased twin population provides additional strain hardening.
Twinning-mediated strain hardening raises hardness and strength without sacrificing ductility.
The Mn-modified alloy will have at least 15% greater yield strength than baseline CoCrFeNiTi.
The Mn-modified alloy will have at least 20% greater Vickers hardness than baseline CoCrFeNiTi.
The Mn-modified alloy will have at least 20% greater deformation-twin density than baseline CoCrFeNiTi.
The uniform elongation of the Mn-modified alloy will remain within 5% of the baseline value.
The hypothesis is limited to similarly processed, homogenized, single-phase FCC alloys tested near 25 °C and 1×10^-3 s^-1.
The proposed mechanism may not apply above approximately 400 °C, above 10^-1 s^-1, or for grain sizes outside 10–200 µm.

contradictions.description: Loading only to approximately 80% of the yield strain remains nominally pre-yield and is incompatible with measuring uniform elongation, post-yield strain hardening, or a substantial deformation-twin population. A tensile test continued through plastic deformation would be required.

The phrase 'substitute 10 at.% Ti with Mn' can mean replacing 10 absolute atomic-percentage points, yielding approximately Co20Cr20Fe20Ni20Ti10Mn10, whereas CoCrFeNiTi0.9Mn0.1 normalizes to Co20Cr20Fe20Ni20Ti18Mn2. The intended composition is therefore ambiguous.

Deformation twins generated during plastic loading can coherently explain increased post-yield work hardening, but they do not directly explain a higher pre-deformation Vickers hardness or necessarily a higher initial yield strength without an additional composition or pre-existing-microstructure mechanism.
